full_judgment:
2. Both the victim Belal Hossain and the informant as petitioners filed an application under section 526 read with section 561A CrPC before the High Court Division praying for transfer of the case from the Court of Sessions Judge at Barisal to the Court of Sessions Judge at Dhaka whereupon a 'Rule was issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.935 of 1997. 

 3. The ground on which the transfer was sought for was that, both the brothers became crippled and unable to move freely from Dhaka to depose in the case. Once they went to depose but the accused-petitioners threatened them with dire consequences if they again go to Barisal to depose in the case and they also threatened the local eye-witnesses not to give evidence. 

 4. Before the High Court Division the Rule was opposed by the accused-petitioners on the ground that it will cause difficulty on the part of the accused persons and the concerned authority to come from Barisal to Dhaka if the Rule is made absolute. The inconvenience of the informant-party should not be a ground for transferring a session’s case from one district to another district. 

 5. In making the Rule absolute by judgment and order dated 27-10-98 a Division Bench of the High Court Division found that it will be most inconvenient for a blind victim and a disabled informant to go to Barisal repeatedly from Dhaka to depose in the case and to secure the attendance of other witnesses. The informant-party has also an apprehension that they will not get a fair and impartial justice in the Court of Barisal. Accordingly, the Rule was made absolute and the session’s case was ordered to be withdrawn and transferred to the 2nd Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka for trial and disposal. 

 6. Mr Moksudur Rahman, learned Advocate for the accused-petitioners, submits that the petition was not maintainable because a petition under section 526 CrPC can only be moved by the parties to the case, i.e. by the accused-petitioners and the State. The informant and his victim brother being merely witnesses have no locus standi to file the petition for transfer. 

 7. This argument is not tenable. The High Court Division can suo motu transfer a sessions case. The informant and his victim brother by preferring the application has merely informed the High Court Division about the state of the circumstances surrounding the concerned session’s case and the High Court Division had complete jurisdiction to exercise its discretion in the matter. 

 9. This argument is also misconceived because on balance the inconvenience of the informant and his victim brother is much higher than that of the accused-petitioners. Besides, they have also an interest in seeing that the eye-witnesses to the occurrence are brought to Dhaka from Barisal and, as such, being crippled persons they are taking upon themselves an onerous burden. 

 10. Mr. Moksudur Rahman finally submits that the session’s case may be transferred to a District adjoining Barisal, but we do not think this is a practical suggestion because the informant and his victim brother in that case will still suffer from the same inconveniences from which they are suffering now.
